items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: If you look at the band, you’d think Wayne and I were on something. We were drunk as skunks.

ctx.x: What public schools did you go to in Detroit?

Well, my mother had adopted Catholicism, and also the first black Catholic Church in this country. They had one…in Chicago, they say there was the first one, but this had a small congregation. She was just the opposite of him from what I gathered, you know? She also died of tuberculosis. Therefore, years later, 1994, when I developed this lung cancer and walked away from it, thanks to God, without Chemo or anything. I’m a poster boy for the cancer society. I don’t smoke or drink. Now, I did drink, but the message…
So, you think it just could have been a vulnerability that was in your family?
